requested.title: A failed deferred-CSS load aborts hydration entirely and permanently marks the stylesheet as loaded
No unobserve path: detached islands that never intersected are retained for the page lifetime, unbounded across server-island reloads
A throwing IntersectionObserver construction escapes connectedCallback, killing the island with no failure stub

rawResponses.rawText:
I've completed the investigation. Here are my verdicts.

```json
[
  {
    "findingId": "F1",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "reasoning": "Both halves of this finding follow directly from the code, and I traced every link. (1) `_doHydrate` sets `this._hydrated = true` at L54 *before* entering the try, then awaits `_doHydrateInner`, whose L94-104 block awaits a promise that `reject`s on `link.onerror`. The rejection unwinds to the L58-65 catch, which only logs and appends `islandFailureStub(...)`; nothing resets `_hydrated` and nothing re-enters `_doHydrate` for a page island (the only caller is `connectedCallback`, and the visible-path observer already self-unobserved at sharedVisibilityObserver.ts:35 before invoking the callback). So a stylesheet failure is terminal: component JS and props were never even requested (the `import()` is at L107-110, after the CSS await), yet the island stays non-interactive. In production the stub is invisible — `ISLAND_FAILURE_CSS` sets `mochi-island-failure { display: none }` unconditionally and the dev rule keys on `[data-message]`, which is omitted when `isDev` is false (islandFailureStub.ts:37-43) — so the user just gets dead SSR markup. The asymmetry with `ServerIsland` is real: that element fire-and-forgets the identical `<link>` injection with no onload/onerror at all (ServerIsland.ts:174-181) while retrying its fetch 10 times (L156/L159). (2) The eager `markLoadedCss(cssUrl)` at L95 is also genuinely wrong on the failure path. The tracker is a process-wide `Set` shared across both inline bundles (sharedCssTracker.ts + the raw `__mochi_loaded_css__` global in ServerIsland.ts:9), and the `css-url` attribute is per-component-path (`__MOCHI_CSS_URL__<islandKey>__` → `cssFileUrls.get(resolvedPath)`, ComponentRegistry.ts:1723-1730), so two instances of the same lazy component — e.g. `{#each items}<Card mochi:hydrate:visible />{/each}` — share one URL. The second instance sees `isLoadedCss` true, skips the block entirely, and hydrates immediately: unstyled if the load failed, FOUC if it is still in flight. This matters because ComponentRegistry.ts:1875-1877 deliberately excludes lazy-island CSS from the page shell (`lazyIslandPaths` → `continue`), so that deferred `<link>` is the island's only stylesheet. Triggers are mundane (flaky network on the stylesheet request, a 404 from a stale hashed URL, any load that fails while the JS would have succeeded), and the maintainers already treat exactly this class of problem as a shipped bug — commit 77b76bc8 fixed 'a plain 404 on the island bundle turned a fully rendered post list and navbar into a blank.' Not fixed in HEAD; the CSS block is untouched by that commit. BUG severity is right."
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F2",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "reasoning": "I verified every step of the retention chain. `observeVisible` is the module's sole export and its sole caller is HydratableIsland.ts:43; a repo-wide grep for `unobserve`/`disconnect` finds only the self-unobserve at sharedVisibilityObserver.ts:35 (reached solely when `e.isIntersecting` is true) plus unrelated observers in MochiCaptcha and IslandsPanel. There is no `unobserveVisible`, and the pooled observer is pinned in a `globalThis` Map (`pinGlobal('__mochi_visibility_pool__')`) for the realm's lifetime, so it is permanently strongly reachable — and it in turn strongly holds every observation target (the file's own comment at L8-12 concedes this). Because the observed node is `this.firstElementChild || this`, its parent pointers retain the whole detached subtree, and the WeakMap entry at L48 stays live since its key is strongly reachable. The churn mechanism the comment assumed away exists: `ServerIsland._reload` → `_fetchContent` assigns `this.innerHTML = html` (ServerIsland.ts:187) after `_unmountChildren` (L71-79), which only bumps `_generation` and calls `_unmount?.()` — undefined for an island that never hydrated — and never touches the observer. So a named `mochi:defer` island (public, documented API: `reloadDeferredIsland`, deferInvalidation.ts:61, docs/70-server-islands.md:70-139) whose rendered content includes a below-the-fold `mochi:hydrate:visible` child leaks one full detached subtree per reload and adds one more permanent observation target each time. The nesting shape is supported and documented ('A server island's content is a full render, so it can contain mochi:hydrate islands'), the endpoint ships the bootstrap that defines the element (Mochi.ts:1684-1687), and the preprocessor's nested-hydration guard (ComponentRegistry.ts:957-979) only blocks hydratables inside *hydratable* subtrees, not inside server islands. The finding's final observation is also correct and is what makes it unbounded: a detached target computes an empty intersection rect, so `isIntersecting` is never true and the L35-37 cleanup is unreachable for exactly the elements that leak. Supporting evidence that the assumption was never revisited: sharedVisibilityObserver.ts was last touched in f7bcd712 (#158), while `reloadDeferredIsland` landed later in 67bc3152 (#312) — the comment even says 'revisit if islands churn faster than expected.' Narrow preconditions keep this at BUG rather than higher."
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F3",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "BUG",
    "reasoning": "The control-flow claim is exactly right and I found no mitigation anywhere. `observeVisible` passes `rootMargin` straight into `new IntersectionObserver(cb, { rootMargin })` (L25-41) with no coercion or try/catch, and its caller does only `options.rootMargin || '0px'` (HydratableIsland.ts:43) inside `connectedCallback`, which is outside the `_doHydrate` try/catch at HydratableIsland.ts:56-65. Per the IntersectionObserver spec the constructor throws a SyntaxError when rootMargin cannot be parsed as 1-4 length-percentage values, so the throw escapes the custom-element reaction: the island never hydrates, no `<mochi-island-failure>` stub is appended, `_hydrated` stays false with nothing to retry it, and there is no framework-level `window.onerror`/`unhandledrejection` listener anywhere in packages/mochi — so the only signal is a console entry. The value really is author-supplied and render-time, not a compile-time literal: svelteAstPreprocess.ts:253 and :388 emit `hydrate-options={JSON.stringify(<author expression>)}` verbatim, and the docs state the option is 'forwarded to IntersectionObserver' (60-lazy-hydration.md:21). Two caveats that I weighed but that do not overturn the finding. First, the headline trigger `rootMargin: 200` *is* caught by svelte-check, since `MochiHydrateVisibleOptions.rootMargin` is typed `string` and `mochi-svelte.d.ts` widens every component's props with `MochiDirectives`; the un-mitigated trigger is the invalid-*string* case the finding also names (`'200'`, `'20 px'`), which type-checks cleanly and throws identically. Second, the sub-claim that the number case keys the pool `Map` with a non-string is wrong in that specific case: the constructor at L25 throws before `pool.set` at L43 ever runs (an array value such as `['0px']` would do it, but that is contrived). The core defect stands and is a genuine robustness asymmetry — every other island failure path in this framework produces a logged error plus a stub, and the same unguarded shape repeats at ServerIsland.ts:30/44 where `_loaded = true` is already set at L27, leaving a deferred island on its fallback forever. Impact is limited to self-inflicted authoring mistakes (the value is not attacker-influenced), so BUG is the correct severity rather than anything higher."
  }
]
```

**Summary:** all three findings confirmed as true positives at BUG severity.

- **F1** — verified end-to-end: `_hydrated` is set before the try, the CSS promise rejects on `onerror`, the catch is terminal, and the production stub is `display:none`. The eager `markLoadedCss` is independently wrong, and it matters because `ComponentRegistry` deliberately excludes lazy-island CSS from the page shell, so the deferred `<link>` is the only source of those styles. Two instances of the same lazy component share one `css-url`, so the sibling-unstyled path is reachable.
- **F2** — the retention chain holds: the pooled observer lives in a `globalThis` Map forever and strongly holds targets, `ServerIsland._unmountChildren` deliberately handles only the Svelte-root leak, and the detached target can never intersect so the self-cleanup is unreachable. The `reloadDeferredIsland` churn mechanism (#312) postdates the "bounded by page lifetime" comment (#158), which is why the assumption went stale.
- **F3** — the throw genuinely escapes `connectedCallback` with no stub and no global error handler. I trimmed two over-claims in my reasoning: `rootMargin: 200` would be caught by `svelte-check` (the real unguarded trigger is an invalid *string*), and the non-string Map key never happens in the number case because the constructor throws first.
